entities.name: 4 cm limb discrepancy
observations: Projected mature discrepancy of 4 cm is generally managed with contralateral growth arrest rather than observation or primary lengthening.

entities.name: Left femur tibia epiphysiodesis
observations: For a projected mature discrepancy of approximately 4 cm, recommended treatment is epiphysiodesis of the distal femoral and proximal tibial physes of the longer limb, timed around puberty onset plus 6 months.

entities.name: Physeal stapling
observations: Stapling or tension-band growth modulation may be reversible but is less predictable and is not clearly superior to accurately timed permanent epiphysiodesis.

entities.name: Limb lengthening
observations: Primary lengthening is less attractive for a projected 4 cm discrepancy because it is more invasive and generally reserved for larger discrepancies or inadequate remaining growth.
